title: what tantra actually is
tomorrow: can a busy parent's ordinary day be a spiritual path?

segments.voice: Yesterday, what tantra actually is held bhoga and yoga, enjoyment and discipline, in one hand. Today, the week looks back, and a goddess worries about people in a hurry.

Some cookbooks give two versions of the big holiday dish: the all-day one, and the weeknight one, for people with jobs and kids and a tired evening. Nobody calls the weeknight version fake. In the Mahanirvana Tantra, the goddess Parvati worries about something like that. Looking ahead to a hard age, she sees people restless, short on time and strength. The old Vedic rites are long and exacting. How will they find their way?
screen: `THE WEEKNIGHT VERSION.` → `PARVATI WORRIES.` → `HOW WILL THEY FIND THE WAY?`

segments.voice: Shiva doesn't wave the worry away. In the book's telling, he praises her question, because she asks it for everyone's good. The world, he says, moves through ages, down to this one, the Kali age, when life is harder. For this age, he gives the teaching of the Tantras. So here, tantra doesn't present itself as a secret for a daring few. It presents itself as a mercy, sized for ordinary, struggling people. Now hold the week up. A seed syllable, the deity in sound, handed on. A yantra, the deity in shape, walked from the gates to the dot. Shiva and Shakti, two voices, never apart. A reputation, answered by a Tantra's own warning. A temple's care, in order, every day. And a verse that holds enjoyment and discipline in one hand. Each uses the world's own stuff, sound, shape, taste, flame, time, as the way in. And this book says why it was given at all: because someone asked how ordinary people could still get there.
screen: `SHIVA PRAISES THE QUESTION.` · `A TEACHING FOR THE KALI AGE.` · `A MERCY, NOT A SECRET.` · `A WEEK OF SOUND, SHAPE, TASTE.` · then, large: `SIZED FOR ORDINARY PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes if that's comfortable, and let one piece of this week come back on its own: a sound, a shape, a taste, a lamp. Rest with whichever arrives first, breathing slowly, and let it be enough.
What tantra actually is: here, a teaching the Mahanirvana Tantra says was given for a hurried age, out of care.
Carry this: what tantra actually is, a mercy sized for a hard age. A week, gathered.
